purpose: Separate what an authority establishes from inference, critique, empirical claims, and normative judgment.
analysis_rules: A critique of judicial reasoning must not be represented as a judicial holding.
Institutional-bias claims require evidence beyond the mere existence of a protective outcome.
Policy preferences must be distinguished from statutory purpose expressly identified by the Legislature or court.
Calling an argument a fallacy requires identifying the inference and explaining why its form is defective in context.
Purposive statutory interpretation is not itself an appeal-to-consequences fallacy; analyze the authorized interpretive methodology first.
Procedural absence, such as a nonappearing party, may limit the adversarial record but does not by itself establish judicial bias.
Broad doctrinal claims require comparison across authorities rather than extrapolation from one case.
When evidence is insufficient, classify the proposition as unresolved rather than increasing rhetorical certainty.
